sentences.text:
Applicant :- Yusuf
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Javed Husain Khan,Ramanuj Pandey

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.

1. Heard Shri Imran Khan (A/I 0084/2012), advocate holding brief of Shri Ramanuj Pandey,
learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.K. Srivastava, learned AGA for the State.2.
2.

This application under Section 528 BNSS has been filed by the applicant to quash the impugned Charge Sheet No. 495 of 2024 dated 28.08.2024 filed in a Case Crime No. 173 of 2024 under section 452, 376, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Banda and the cognizance order/summon dated 25.11.2024 passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Banda.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that a first information report was lodged by the opposite party no. 2 against the applicant on 13.03.2024, FIR No. 0173, under Sections 452, 376,
504, 506 IPC with an allegation that though the applicant is a married woman, however, the applicant herein who claimed to be a doctor and a tenant of a house adjacent to the house of the opposite party no. 2 used to exhibit indecent behaviour and gesture and further he on 14.11.2023 came to the house of the opposite party no. 2 at 8'o clock and made inquiries about the husband of the opposite party no. 2 and when the mother of opposite party no. 2 had gone to bring some snacks Yusuf vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121067256/

sentences.text: then he not only touched the vital parts but also committed bad acts.
Complaint was also lodged and thereafter post investigation, charge-sheet has been submitted against the applicant.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that very basis of lodging of the first information report itself stands eroded, particularly, when the applicant is not a doctor or a medical practitioner but a journalist and further he had made complaints regarding illegal constructions against one Faiz Ulla who happens to be complainant's uncles regarding illegal constructions and when the construction was stopped then that became the motivating factor for lodging of the first information report.
4. Submission is that there happens to be newspapers cuttings to substantiate the allegation of the applicant against the opposite party no. 2.

He also seeks to rely upon an order passed in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13579 of 2024 wherein interim protection was accorded till submission of the charge-sheet under Section 173(2) of the Cr.P.C.
5.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13579 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned AGA while countering the submission so sought to be made by the learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the first information report pinpointed allegations of commission of the offences have been levelled and further the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. also supports the prosecution theory.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the records carefully.
7. Apparently, in the first information report, allegation has been leveled for exhibiting indecent behaviour and also committed offences of bad act.
The prosecution story stands supported by the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim.

8. The question as to whether what would be the stage of considering the defence with relation to the theory propounded by the applicant regarding complaint made for raising illegal constructions by the uncle of the opposite party no. 2 is concerned, the stage has not arrived as the same may be the matter of defence.

This Court at this stage is to just evaluate the things while taking into account the allegations as well as the statements made under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
9.
In view of the said discussion, no case is made out.
Accordingly, the application stands dismissed.
10. At this juncture, learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant shall be preferring a discharge application.
11. In the opinion of the Court, if a discharge application is maintainable under law, is preferred then this Court has no reason to disbelieve that the same shall be decided with most expedition.

Order Date :- 5.6.2025 A. Prajapati  Yusuf vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121067256/
